engagement_title: Gable & Grove spring season kit: build an honest before and after library from five finished jobs, recover the lost mark as artwork that holds on a deep green yard sign, rebuild the retired printer's project cards, and hand back the quote pack and the social set
vertical: Home and property services: premium exterior renovation and garden build, five person firm (Litchfield Hills, Connecticut)
real_brief_anchor: Anchor: the Upwork home services branding brief in the ledger's grounding_note, from a new home services company that had a logo mark and wanted it cleaned up and rolled out consistently across trucks, uniforms, yard signs, social and print, laundered here to the fictional Gable & Grove Home Services (no real company, person or trademark appears anywhere; the brand, the crew, the jobs and all copy are invented for this benchmark). The killed spec was fake on two counts: every deliverable was a one click operation, and it asked for a trace of a photograph of printed artwork as though that were a clean input. The fuller commission this firm genuinely has is the season kit, because a before and after library is worthless without the collateral it feeds, the project card run is a real record per page job rebuildable from the press file the retired printer left, and the mark has to survive from a shirt to a yard sign or it is not artwork, it is a picture of a logo.
client_one_liner: Everything we sell we sell twice, on the site and on somebody's kitchen table, and right now we are selling it with phone snaps, a logo file the sign writer emailed us once, and project cards from a printer who has retired.
client_brief:
Gable & Grove Home Services, spring season kit

We do full exterior renovations and garden builds in the Litchfield Hills, mostly between forty five and a hundred and twenty thousand dollars a project. Everything we sell, we sell twice: once on the website, and once out of a quote pack on somebody's kitchen table.

We have five finished jobs from last season and photographs of all of them, before and after, some off my phone and some off our estimator's camera. They are a mess. The befores need to stay honest, because that is the entire point of a before, and the afters need to look like what we actually deliver. We are not an HGTV company. If the afters look like a supermarket flyer, the people we sell to will price us at eight thousand dollars and call somebody else.

We need those pairs for the site and for the quote pack, and we need the pergola from the Ridge Road job pulled out cleanly so we can put it on things. It is the best thing we have ever built.

Our mark is a problem. The sign writer who drew it is gone and all we have is a picture file he emailed once, plus a photograph of our own truck door. We need it back as proper artwork we can hand to anybody: the sign shop, the shirt printer, whoever. It has to work everywhere from a shirt to a yard sign, and our yard signs are the deep green.

We also need the project cards. Our old printer ran one per finished job for the quote packs and the showroom board. He has retired, we have the file he sent to press, and we now have more jobs than cards.

Then the quote pack itself, the before and after module for the site, and the social sizes. All of it editable by us, because prices change and I am not paying twice.

Finally, a note on what you did, and why the befores are treated differently from the afters.
price_band_and_audience: A firm charging 45,000 to 120,000 dollars a project, selling to households aged 45 to 65 with old houses and long time horizons, at a kitchen table against two other bids. The band is load-bearing and it points at restraint: at this price the afters read cool, calm and material, with real neutral stone, deep honest blacks, one photograph doing the work, generous white space in the quote pack and a mark that behaves like a maker's stamp rather than a sales badge. The same brief for an 8,000 dollar handyman outfit would correctly be brighter, warmer, more saturated, busier, with four photographs a page, a starburst price and a phone number in the biggest type on the sheet, and shipping that here loses the job on sight because it tells the buyer this firm competes on price. Pushed the other way into a black ground with gold rules it reads as a developer, which this buyer distrusts more than a flyer. A dishonestly improved before fails at any band, because it destroys the only proof the firm has. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.typography: A quiet display serif for the mark and headings paired with a restrained humanist sans for scope, prices and captions. Legible, unhurried, no starbursts and no oversized phone number.

brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark is a problem the firm names openly: the sign writer who drew it is gone, and all that survives is a picture file he emailed once and a photograph of the mark hand painted on the firm's truck door. The project cards survive only as the retired printer's press PDF. Yard signs print in the deep Grove Green.
brand_identity.values: Honest befores are non negotiable, and the finish should read as ordered restraint rather than as an improved photograph.

assets_supplied.name: job_photos/ (14 frames across 5 jobs, approx 1600 x 1200 to 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Before and after captures of five completed exterior renovation and garden jobs, shot across a season on the owner's phone and the estimator's camera in whatever light the site had.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Five finished jobs, before and after. Some off my phone, some off the estimator's camera. They are a mess."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the fourteen are screenshots the office pulled out of a text thread rather than the original captures, so they carry a fraction of the pixels of everything else and cannot reach the library's delivery size without interpolation. On the Ridge Road job the before and the after were shot months apart from slightly different standing positions in different light, and the limestone runs to opposite sides of neutral in the two frames in a way that is not legible in either frame alone; that job's after also has a pale limestone pergola standing against a flat overcast sky of very nearly its own luminance.

assets_supplied.name: mark_sources/ (mark_flat.png, truck_door.jpg)
assets_supplied.kind: Two sources for the same lost mark: a raster file the sign writer emailed the firm years ago, and a photograph of the mark hand painted on the door of the firm's truck, shot in the yard.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All we have of the logo. The picture file he sent us once, and a photo of our own truck."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The emailed file is a screen resolution export of the mark sitting on a white plate with a soft drop shadow baked into it, and the wordmark is disjoint lettering, so the obvious knockout route returns a grey plate and a couple of surviving letters while reporting success. The truck door is a graphic on an object, where a prompt naming the door pulls the selection to the door rather than to the paint, and the mark itself carries one narrow open counter in the initial and a hairline rule beneath the wordmark.

assets_supplied.name: projectcard_2025_print.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The retired printer's flat press PDF for the project cards, A6 portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries a job name, a location line, a scope line, a season line and a placed job photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card he ran for the quote packs and the showroom board. We only have what went to press."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The photo frame he drew is close to square, which the printed card never advertises because the photograph he happened to place in it was square, so a wide crop bound to that frame is centre cropped by the frame and quietly loses whatever sits at its edges, which on these jobs is the finished feature. The card's copy lines also arrive as one continuous flow rather than as separate frames, and the mapping readout does not report every run in it.

assets_supplied.name: projects.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the estimating spreadsheet, one row per completed job, with columns for job name, location, scope, season and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every job we finished last season. Eleven rows, five of them the ones we photographed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One finished job is entered twice by two estimators under two different job names with two different season values, so shipping both puts the same pergola on two cards in one quote pack. One row is a job whose homeowner withheld permission to publish, which is recorded in the owner's notes and nowhere in the export, and the photo column names files that do not exist yet because this engagement produces them.

assets_supplied.name: brand_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from the owner: the deep green the yard signs are printed in, what the mark means to him, the price band and the clientele, and what he means when he says HGTV.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we want to look, and what we do not want to look like."

acceptance_bar: The afters read as ONE firm's finish across five jobs shot in different light: one white point on the stone, one black point, one degree of correction, one crop logic. A job that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.

The befores stay honest. Any correction applied to a before is legibility only, is disclosed, and does not flatter the site. A before that has been quietly improved fails the whole library regardless of how good the after looks.
Every delivered pair is genuinely a pair: the same site, comparable framing, and no visible divergence in the colour of the same material across the two frames.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. If a pair cannot reach the library size at its own resolution, we are told the size it CAN reach rather than being handed interpolated pixels.
The isolated pergola is clean at the edge where the stone meets the sky, judged on a contrasting ground rather than on a checkerboard preview.

The mark is delivered as artwork, not a picture of artwork: placeable, scalable, transparent where it should be transparent, and intact at real reproduction size on the firm's own deep green, including its counter and its hairline rule.
Both mark sources are handled on their own merits and the reasoning is stated. A route that works on one and produces a substrate shaped blob on the other is not a route.

Exactly one project card per publishable job, no duplicate card and no card for a job we are not allowed to show. If the number shipped is not the number the export implies, the note says which row was withheld and why.
Every card's photograph is the job named on the card, and the finished feature is still in the photograph after the card's own frame has had its way with it.
Each per-project file contains the job its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back in.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The quote pack, the before and after module, the social set and the yard sign come back as a native editable document we can change prices in, with every photograph actually visible, the scope block as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.
Nothing in the kit reads as a supermarket flyer or as developer marketing at our band.

A written note: what was applied to each frame, why the befores differ from the afters, how each mark source was handled, every job row questioned and its resolution, and every resize any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including element extraction
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (global and masked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor), image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The library, the pergola isolation and the recovery of the mark, all of which live on this one family (image_vectorize is a Photoshop family tool here, not an Illustrator surface). It holds five differently lit jobs to one finish while deliberately holding the befores back, isolates a pale feature against a sky of similar luminance, triages two mark sources that need opposite routes, and produces the trace plus the raster prep that is the only tuning lever vectorize has. Selections come back fully binary with no intermediate values, and there is no measurement anywhere, so every judgement is made by looking at what returned.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The project card run for the quote packs and the showroom board. The retired printer's press file becomes a live merge template, the estimating export becomes the data source after reconciliation, and the run produces the cards, the per-project single files, and the proofs. The card's real frame bounds and its true story text have to be read out of the exported interchange file rather than assumed from the printed card or trusted from a convenience readout, and the placeholder inventory confirmed by round trip rather than by a success message.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The quote pack at true physical dimensions, the before and after web module, the mixed canvas social set (square, four by five and nine by sixteen in one export) and the yard sign at its real physical size on the firm's deep green, all as one native editable document. Every photograph inlined as image data, the recovered mark inlined as SVG markup so it lands as real editable vector rather than a flattened picture, the scope block as a genuine table, family and weight declared per text element, each root declaring its own canvas.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the quote pack, the module, the social set and the yard sign, and the only place the agent's typographic authorship exists, since no font from this surface can reach the printed project card. The pairing is the agent's own art direction against a maker's stamp rather than a sales badge, the numeric weight per family is non-standard, one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one honest non job image the quote pack needs for its how we work page, since the firm has no photograph of materials or crew and nothing may be fabricated: a licensed, IP clean, camera scale still that must be declared as stock. The Boards half persists the shortlisted pairs for the owner and the estimator to sign off before eleven cards and a quote pack are committed, placed within the twelve per call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: project cards to the merge surface, quote pack, module, social set and yard sign to authored canvases, photography and the mark to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The card is record per page against a layout the showroom board already locks in; the quote pack is free form and must stay editable, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the fourteen job frames, both mark sources, the press PDF, the estimating export and the owner's notes, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by job, by role and by state, because the same frame will exist in four states before the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by job and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen and pair each before with its after, noting light, apparent capture device, framing, what material dominates each pair and how much edge each frame has to spare.
trajectory.judgement: A pair is a claim about one site, so what the two frames share and where they diverge is the thing being assessed, not how good either looks alone.
trajectory.produces: A per pair triage note: job, light, framing, dominant material and edge margin.

trajectory.action: Correct the befores only as far as honesty allows, deciding and recording what honest means at this band.
trajectory.judgement: The before is the firm's only proof, so the line between making a phone snap legible and quietly improving the site is the single most consequential craft decision in the engagement and the client has already named the failure.
trajectory.produces: Legibility corrected befores with a per frame parameter log and a stated standard.

trajectory.action: Fix one finish target and bring every after toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Five jobs shot across a season in different light have to arrive at one white point and one black point, which means five different routes to one destination rather than one batched move, and the destination is set by a band that punishes saturation.
trajectory.produces: Five graded afters at source scale with a per job parameter log.

trajectory.action: Derive the web three by two and square crops of every pair and lay each finished pair side by side at one size, reading confidence and tradeoffs on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across five jobs, not ten good crops, and the tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped or that an output was interpolated toward the two times cap. A pair is judged as a pair at the only moment that comparison exists.
trajectory.produces: Paired crops with their tradeoff records and a pair by pair judgement.

trajectory.action: Isolate the Ridge Road pergola for the hero and inspect the result on a contrasting ground rather than on a transparency preview.
trajectory.judgement: Which isolation instrument suits this subject is a judgement about the boundary, and the tool exposes no threshold, no matte control and no confidence, so what its detector did on this frame can only be seen by looking at the returned edge against something it contrasts with.
trajectory.produces: An isolated pergola on a plain ground plus a transparent version, inspected on a real ground.

trajectory.action: Triage the two mark sources and take each down its own route, naming the ink and its own visual properties rather than the surface it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: The emailed plate and the painted door look like the same job and are not: naming the substrate pulls a selection to the substrate, and a subject knockout on disjoint lettering collapses to a few letters while reporting success.
trajectory.produces: A clean positive plate of the mark from whichever source survives, with the reasoning for both routes recorded.

trajectory.action: Trace the prepared plate, then do the vector hygiene by hand: inject a viewBox, strip the full canvas background rectangle, and check the counter and the hairline rule.
trajectory.judgement: The trace takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation that precedes it, and an untouched trace is neither scalable nor transparent no matter how clean it looks.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus the raster prep that produced it.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the one honest non job still the quote pack needs, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose light and whose blacks can live beside five graded jobs, not the moodiest thumbnail, and declare it as stock. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale still, graded toward the finish target.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's and has to read as a maker's stamp at a kitchen table against two other bids, not as a sales badge. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the quote pack at true physical dimensions, the before and after module, the square, four by five and nine by sixteen social canvases and the yard sign at its real size on the deep green, inlining every photograph as image data and the mark as SVG markup.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air this band takes and how the mark is scaled and placed on its own ground.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole kit, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then look: verify canvas one from the document's rendition and the rest from the returned per canvas markup, including how the mark resolved.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, the rendition shows the first artboard only, and a traced mark arrives as many loose shapes rather than one object.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the estimating export against the owner's notes, normalise it into a merge shaped data file with an at prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the chosen after images and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation: one job is entered twice under two names, one job may not be shown at all, and the photo column points at files this engagement produces. What is the agent's call and what is the owner's is a decision, and consent is not one of them.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded card images, the image map and a list of job questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory and bounds, then reconstruct each frame's true story text from its concatenated content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy and the photo frame's true aspect are properties of the retired printer's document, not of the printed card, and every offset must be computed from the document rather than from a convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every copy field plus the photo frame, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence, and ordering any rows that share a uid so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per row images bound, then render the card run and the proofs at true print resolution from that document, and produce the per-project single files, naming each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per-record branch open, and identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that puts the wrong job in a quote pack.
trajectory.produces: The project card run, print resolution proofs, and per-project files verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card at trim rather than at proof scale, checking each line and what the card's own photo frame did to the crop it was given.
trajectory.judgement: A wrongly bound photograph and a feature cropped away by the frame both look like success at the API boundary and both look plausible on a screen scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A card by card reconciliation against the reconciled roster.

trajectory.action: Build the sign off board of shortlisted pairs and the mark within the placement cap, re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, vector is not accepted there, and the note has to state the honesty standard applied to the befores in the client's own terms.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the Ridge Road pair still reads as one site once both frames are finished and adjacent. The before and the after were shot months apart from slightly different standing positions in different light, and the limestone in the two runs to opposite sides of neutral. Neither frame looks wrong on its own, and neither looks wrong beside the other four jobs; the divergence only exists as a property of the pair, at one size, side by side, after both have been taken to the finish target. There is no eyedropper and no histogram anywhere in the connector, so it cannot be predicted from either frame and can only be seen once the pair is assembled.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the comparison requires both frames finished and cropped, and care cannot prevent it: bringing each frame correctly to the set target is exactly what makes the divergence legible. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the befores must stay honest and the afters must look like the firm's finish, which are the client's goals; no asset note, no earlier step and no deliverable says anything about the stone or about how the two frames relate. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the responses available are a confined correction on the stone alone, a re-crop toward the framing the two frames actually share, or dropping the job from the library, and each is a different decision with different downstream consequences.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Judge the pair adjacent at one size rather than each frame alone, then either confine a correction to the stone (accepting that a binary selection cannot blend at the planting boundary and inspecting the result at full resolution), or re-derive both crops toward the framing the two genuinely share, or set that job aside and re-pick which pair leads the module and the quote pack. Any of the three re-flows into the social set and into which after is bound to that job's project card.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The firm's flagship pair goes on the website and into every quote pack showing limestone that is warm grey before and cool grey after, which a buyer at a kitchen table reads as a different house, and the before and after claim, which is the only proof this firm has, quietly stops being believed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the isolation actually did to the pergola's edge where the stone meets the sky. The pale limestone stands against a flat overcast sky of very nearly its own luminance, and the tool exposes no threshold, no matte control, no confidence value and no warning: it succeeds, returns a cutout whose overall silhouette is right, and the transparency preview looks clean because a checkerboard behind a pale edge hides exactly this. Whether the detector took the rafter tails and the balustrade with the sky is a property of this frame and this boundary, and it becomes visible only when the cutout is put on a ground it contrasts with, at full resolution.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, and the agent cannot simply do it right first time because there is no parameter to set: the same call is the only call, and what it did is observable only afterwards. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the pergola pulled out cleanly, which is the goal, and the acceptance line about a clean edge is the client's own standard, not a disclosure that this edge is at risk. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different instrument entirely, a positive selection of the structure by its own visual properties then an inverted knockout or a bounded crop, and possibly a different hero if the boundary will not give.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the cutout on a contrasting ground rather than on transparency, and where the edge has been bitten, rebuild the isolation through an explicit selection of the structure and its inversion, or fall back to a solid ground knockout that keeps the edge and gives up transparency, then re-judge the hero at the size the yard sign and the quote pack actually use it and re-place it in both.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The best thing this firm has ever built goes on a yard sign, a quote pack cover and the site with its rafter tails eaten off against a deep green ground, which is instantly legible to anybody who has looked at a pergola and reads as carelessness by the firm that built it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at real reproduction size on the firm's own deep green. The trace is clean at the size it was made, where the narrow counter in the initial is open and the hairline rule under the wordmark is a rule. What that same geometry does when it is placed at yard sign scale on a saturated dark ground, and how the importer resolves it into the document, is a different question: the counter can fill visually against the green and the hairline can drop below the weight at which it reads as a line rather than as an artefact. The trace tool takes no options at all, so nothing about this is adjustable at the point of tracing, and the only channel that reports what actually happened is the returned per canvas markup and the rendition.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the ground, the scale and the trace all have to exist before the question exists, and care cannot settle it: a mark that is manifestly clean at canvas size gives no signal about a dark ground at sign size. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mark has to work from a shirt to a yard sign and names the green, which is the client's requirement; nothing in the assets, the steps or the deliverables says anything about what the trace does to the counter or the rule. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix lives three steps back in the raster preparation, because the trace has no parameters, so the response is to re-prepare the plate and trace again, which is a different piece of work.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Look at the mark on its real ground at its real size rather than at authoring scale, and if the counter closes or the rule fails, go back to the raster preparation (a tighter or differently prompted plate, a different source between the emailed file and the painted door, a cleaner polarity) and trace again, then re-inject the viewBox, strip the background rectangle again, re-place it and re-export, and record the smallest reproduction the delivered artwork actually holds at.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The firm hands the artwork to a sign shop and a shirt printer as the definitive mark, and every yard sign in the Litchfield Hills carries a filled initial and a broken rule, which is worse than the situation the firm started in because it is now committed and paid for.

deliverables.name: Before and after library, five matched pairs
deliverables.spec: Five pairs where the befores are corrected only for legibility against a stated and disclosed standard and the afters are brought to one finish target across jobs shot in different light, each pair genuinely a pair in framing and in the colour of its shared materials. Delivered as web three by two and square crops from one crop logic, every output at or below its source dimensions, with any pair that cannot reach the library size at its own resolution named along with the size it can reach, plus a per frame parameter log.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns a beautiful garden that nobody built. IDENTITY is the whole product: a before and after is a claim that THIS firm did THIS work at THIS house, and a generated after in a quote pack is not a design shortcut, it is fraud in front of a homeowner. The mark is the firm's actual mark, painted on its actual truck, and a redrawn approximation is a different company's logo handed to a sign shop. SPEC: the firm needs one A6 card per publishable job binding four named fields verbatim with the right job's photograph, per-project files each containing the job they claim, proofs at true print resolution, and delivered images that never exceed their sources. EDITABILITY: the quote pack is defined by being editable because prices move. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this pair still read as one site, did this knockout keep the rafter tails, does this counter stay open on green at sign size.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted (image_vectorize counted as Photoshop family, not as an Illustrator surface, and no dead vector or video tool anywhere), no banned capability. IMAGING: apply_adjustments global and masked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, remove_background transparent and with backgroundColor, fill_area, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor, and vectorize are all verified headless, as is the full extract and reuse chain select, invert, crop to bounds, vectorize, inject viewBox, strip path 0, inline into HTML, export. The three checkpoints rest on documented facts rather than invention: there is NO measurement anywhere in the family, so a divergence between two frames of the same material can only be seen by putting them adjacent; remove_background exposes no threshold, no matte and no confidence and is documented collapsing on boundaries its detector reads as ambiguous (a solid disc on an enclosed interior, two surviving letters on disjoint lettering), so what it did to an edge is only observable against a contrasting ground; and image_vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL, with the documented consequence that all tuning must happen in the raster prep, which is what makes a re-trace a genuine three step return rather than a re-run. The documented prompt gate (naming the substrate selects the substrate, naming the ink's own colour, medium and form selects the ink) carries the two source triage, and both failure modes return success. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored, frame granularity and bounds from a PDF are documented as not under your control, and the mapping readout's text content is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. Per row image binding through an at prefixed column plus an image map is verified visually. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at exactly 96 dpi, real tables, inline SVG arriving as native editable vector shapes, and a genuine editable document are all verified; the rendition shows PAGE 1 ONLY so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; payload routed by uploaded URL. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve per call board cap with 201 meaning partial and vector unsupported there. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text or replace_image or animate_design, no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no batch above 20.
